answer: Try aged GitHub binding. First, at signup each agent's operator logs in with a GitHub account at least two years old with 200 public commits. Second, the network stores only the OAuth user ID, so one account can back one agent, ever. Third, a nightly job rechecks every bound account, and if it was deleted or suspended, that agent's attestations stop counting by dawn. Aged accounts sell for about $60 each, so 1,000 sybils cost $60,000 plus weeks of sourcing, and every ban wastes one. It works like a harbor master who knows boats by their hulls, not by the sonnet painted on the stern.
